land.text: 'It comprises the main southern island of Unguja (also known as Zanzibar), the smaller northern island of Pemba, and numerous surrounding islets.'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks: its Sultanate of Zanzibar row runs to 1966 and its Tanzania shape adds the islands only in 1967. The islands were this republic from 12 January to April 1964. The page gives no area.

region.text: 'It comprises the main southern island of Unguja (also known as Zanzibar), the smaller northern island of Pemba, and numerous surrounding islets.'

ledger.note: 12 January 1964: the revolutionaries proclaim the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba. 'The revolution began on 12 January 1964'; 'The country was renamed the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba', with 'Karume heading the council as President'. The page dates the revolution, not the proclamation itself.

region.text: 'It comprises the main southern island of Unguja (also known as Zanzibar), the smaller northern island of Pemba, and numerous surrounding islets.'

ledger.note: April 1964: Zanzibar unites with Tanganyika. 'On 26 April Karume announced that a union had been negotiated with Tanganyika to form the new country of Tanzania'; the same page also says 'With the merger of Tanganyika and Zanzibar on 23 April'. The Sultanate page: 'In April 1964, the existence of this socialist republic was ended with its union with Tanganyika.'

region.text: 'It comprises the main southern island of Unguja (also known as Zanzibar), the smaller northern island of Pemba, and numerous surrounding islets.'

ledger.note: April 1964: the republic ends in the union. 'In April 1964, the existence of this socialist republic was ended with its union with Tanganyika'; the union formed the 'United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, which became known as Tanzania six months later'. The land goes to Tanzania (identity.successors).

sources.title: Zanzibar Revolution
sources.note: The revolution (12 January 1964), the renaming to the People's Republic of Zanzibar and Pemba, Karume, the union of April 1964 (23 or 26 April), the territory.

sources.title: Sultanate of Zanzibar
sources.note: The end of the socialist republic in April 1964 and the later name Tanzania; Stone Town as the Sultanate's capital.

sources.title: People's Republic of Zanzibar
sources.note: Added by reviewer af-08-j: the state's own article ('a short-lived African state founded in 1964, consisting of the islands of the Zanzibar Archipelago'; infobox 'Zanzibar Revolution: 12 January 1964', 'Merger with Tanganyika: 26 April', 'Capital: Zanzibar City').

notes: A state Cliopatria lacks, written as the direct successor of sultanate-of-zanzibar. It lasted about three and a half months, so a yearly map shows it for 1964 only; af-08-x did not list it. No Wikipedia article was opened under this state's own title (wikipedia and wikidata are null; the Zanzibar Revolution page is the source). The union date conflicts on the Zanzibar Revolution page (23 April merger against 26 April announcement); the dossier gives month 4. Whether the Coastal Strip had any role after 12 December 1963 is covered in the Sultanate and Kenya dossiers. Capital is a bridging judgement. The Tanzania dossier (another part) should take Zanzibar from April 1964.
